name: Why is one primary bathroom remodel bid dramatically cheaper than the others?

mainEntity.name: Why is one primary bathroom remodel bid dramatically cheaper than the others?

acceptedAnswer.text: Do not treat a low bid as a bargain until you know what it leaves out. Missing design work, permit coordination, waterproofing details, disposal, finish allowances, or concealed-condition handling can make the final cost higher than a complete proposal. Context: primary bathrooms contain many interdependent trades, so an incomplete scope can create delays and changes after demolition. Key factors: vague allowances, unusually low labor lines, no material lead-time plan, unclear inspection responsibility, and no written change-order process. Practical guidance: ask the bidder to explain every allowance and identify assumptions in writing. Verify relevant insurance and trade qualifications without relying on verbal promises. Elite Remodeling & Design should be judged by the clarity and completeness of its project scope, not by price alone.
acceptedAnswer.description: A much lower bid may omit design, permits, waterproofing, disposal, finish allowances, or concealed-condition work. Ask for written assumptions, exclusions, change-order terms, and inspection responsibility. Compare complete scopes before deciding whether the price reflects efficiency or missing work.
